lead: Requirement set: NRW corporate plan performance framework, version 2024-25 draft, transcription 1.
Period covered: 2026-01-01 to 2026-12-31. Rendered on 2026-10-06 from the register as it stood that day.
method_note:
Scan runs started in the period: 4. Their funnels are in the first table below.

Final dispositions of those runs' candidates: promoted 10, rejected 6, duplicate 0, reinforcement 4, deferred 1. New candidates nobody has judged yet: 1.

Reports created in the period: 10, of which 5 (50 per cent) came from lanes outside government. The mainstream bias guard asks for this share: a register that skews official misses the earliest signals.

The credibility of those 10 reports, digit by digit, is in the table below. Grades inflate quietly: a consultation is a 3, however official the page.

Instrument version used by the period's runs: 2026.10.0.

Known blind spots, requirements this tool cannot see and holds no active report on: SI9 Impact of partnership approaches, SI11 Organisations acting on the crises, SI12 NRW colleague engagement.

The scan only finds what already talks like the requirements. Biophysical, market, technological and institutional pressures that move a requirement before any publication names it are outside its reach.

Counts of reports are not counts of impact. The register shows what surfaced publicly: at least this much, and known to undercount.

body: This annual strategic assessment sets out the standing picture of the external signals bearing on each requirement in the set, to inform the annual prioritisation exercise.

It is assembled from the register and the standing copy: every sentence is a fixed form filled with counts and titles, and nothing in it is a recommendation. Each requirement's picture counts its active reports (emerging, tracking and reinforced); matured reports are settled context and named separately.
The questions for each well-being objective are drawn from the reports that threaten a requirement or cut both ways. They are questions about the world for the people who set priorities, not advice.
sections.heading: Purpose

body: For each requirement: its coverage status, its active reports by direction and by state, their grading spread, its scanability in the framework's own words, and the active reports with the highest potential impact.
sections.heading: Standing picture by requirement

sections.heading: SI8 Increasing the proportion of the population living in places that will continue to support and contribute to their health and well-being in a changing climate

body: Coverage status: blind spot, from 0 active reports.
By direction: none.
By state: none.
Grading spread: none.

Scanability: low. Evidence is mostly internal to NRW (grants, Area Statements, MoUs, Natur a Ni), but PSB well-being assessments and plans are published on a roughly 5-year cycle: the next assessments are due end 2026 to early 2027. So this is quiet between cycles with a known upcoming window, not permanently blind.

A blind spot is not quiet. A requirement whose evidence public sources cannot see (low or no scanability) and that has no active reports is invisible to this tool, not calm; its silence is not evidence of anything.

body: The audit runs down both axes: the requirements, by the lane each report was found in, and the taxonomy, by the ecosystems, resources and hazard families the reports touch.
sections.heading: Coverage audit

body: Each cell counts the active reports assessed against the requirement that were found in the lane. A row's status comes from the requirement's scanability and its total, so a requirement public sources cannot see reads blind spot, never quiet.
